| [affidavit-pack](../../packs/affidavit-pack/) | projection | deprecated | DEPRECATED, superseded by affidavit-consumer-pack (recorded in lifecycle.toml; [pack] admits only name/version/description). Typed Rust catalog + real executable certify-pipeline logic + reference doc, generated from domain vocabulary for ~/affidavit (crates.io `affidavit` v26.6.22, a cryptographic provenance/receipt engine). Modeled from its README's 'Core Concepts' section: a Receipt is an append-only BLAKE3-chained log of Events, each carrying a Commitment (a BLAKE3 digest of payload data -- payloads themselves are never stored in the receipt). Every CertifyStage/Command triple was hand-verified 2026-07-18 against the actual ~/affidavit README.md on disk (byte-for-byte match, not just 'plausible from prose'), version-pinned via afd:sourceVersion in ontology.ttl. No command-surface enumeration attempted for the other 55 verbs (the README documents 59 canonical verbs total in prose only, no table); this pack covers the receipt data model plus 4 named core verbs, not the full CLI. Generates: (1) src/affidavit_catalog.rs -- reference tables (CERTIFY_STAGES, CORE_VERBS); (2) src/affidavit_certify.rs -- real executable logic: an ontology-order-derived Stage dispatcher (next_stage/is_terminal), plus (round 3, 2026-07-18) two generic domain-independent structural primitives (check_strictly_increasing/check_unique) composed by check_stage() per-stage from the ontology's afd:checksMonotonic/afd:checksUnique boolean facts -- check_continuity() is now a thin named call into that ontology-driven dispatch rather than one hand-written affidavit-specific body, proven against adversarial duplicate/out-of-order inputs plus the composition/dispatch mechanism itself in tests/affidavit_certify_proof.rs; (3) docs/affidavit_reference.md; (4) src/affidavit_lib_wiring.rs (force:true, plain file -- NOT inject-mode; retargeted off src/lib.rs during round 2's cross-pack verification after two other packs collided writing to that same path in a shared consumer) containing `pub mod affidavit_catalog;`/`pub mod affidavit_certify;`, which the consumer must mount with one `include!("affidavit_lib_wiring.rs");` line in their own src/lib.rs -- a disclosed, real remaining consumer-effort step, not 'wires ggen.toml, done'. Both affidavit_catalog.rs/affidavit_certify.rs use freeze_policy=checksum (freeze_slots_dir=.ggen/freeze/affidavit-pack) so a hand-edit to generated output is detected and regeneration is skipped rather than silently clobbered. Round 4 (2026-07-19, real reference found at ~/affidavit -- the actual crate checkout on this machine, not merely its README): the prior rounds above modeled only the CertifyStage labels/order/rejectCondition prose. This round transcribes ~/affidavit's actual `src/types.rs`/`src/chain.rs`/`src/verifier.rs` (v26.6.22, checksummed copies committed read-only at `reference/affidavit_v26.6.22_src/{types,chain,verifier}.rs` -- `shasum -a 256` confirmed byte-identical against the live `~/affidavit/src/*.rs` at copy time) into three new generated modules: `src/affidavit_types.rs` (Blake3Hash/ObjectRef/OperationEvent/Receipt with its forgery-resistant custom Deserialize/CheckOutcome/Verdict/ProfileId/canonical_bytes -- the `Evidence<_,Admitted,_>`/wasm4pm_compat witness-type layer is deliberately NOT transcribed, out of this pack's ontology scope), `src/affidavit_chain.rs` (real BLAKE3 rolling-chain-hash ChainAssembler/recompute_chain/content_address/serialize_receipt/deserialize_receipt, byte-for-byte port of the real algorithm, not a paraphrase), `src/affidavit_verifier.rs` (the real 6-function stage_decode/stage_check_format/stage_chain_integrity/stage_continuity/stage_verify_commitments/stage_evaluate_profile + verify() dispatch, identical control flow to the reference). That repo independently evolved exactly this shape by hand -- lib/ash_r2rml/resource.ex (AshR2RML.Resource: sections :r2rml/:sparql, entities Class/Subject/Property/Reference/Graph, transformer AshR2RML.Resource.Persist, verifier AshR2RML.Resource.Verify, Info module AshR2RML.Resource.Info), lib/mix/tasks/ash_r2rml.install.ex (Igniter installer), lib/ash_r2rml/reactor_pipeline.ex + lib/ash_r2rml/reactor/steps/*.ex (compile -> verify_alignment/evaluate_differential -> attach_provenance -> apply_policy -> render_r2rml_turtle), and lib/ash_r2rml/ggen.ex (a construct_only compiler boundary that returns a path/content graph + receipt and never touches the filesystem itself -- ggen owns rendering/actuation, this pack's manufactured code never does). Two gaps in the golden specimen this pack deliberately does NOT repeat: 1. ash_r2rml's installer (lib/mix/tasks/ash_r2rml.install.ex) only adds the formatter plugin and then prints manual "add `extensions: [AshR2RML.Resource]` yourself" instructions via Igniter.add_notice -- ALWAYS, no matter how it's invoked, because it never asks for a target module. This pack's installer template performs the real Igniter.Project.Module patch (adds the `extensions: [...]` entry and a starter DSL block) whenever the caller passes `--target MyApp.SomeResource` -- one command, not a README-driven manual step, for that invocation. Without `--target` it falls back to the same disclosed manual notice ash_r2rml always uses (there's no way to know which module to patch otherwise) -- so the upgrade over ash_r2rml is real but conditional on `--target`, not universal across every invocation. (Confirmed via audit 2026-08-26: an earlier draft of this note overclaimed "installation is one command" as if it held unconditionally.) 2. The embedded pack at ash_r2rml/priv/ggen/ash-r2rml-pack/pack.toml declares `name = "ash-r2ml-pack"` (missing the second "r" against its own directory name "ash-r2rml-pack") -- a real, confirmed naming typo. This pack's own name is spelled and verified correctly and is a distinct pack, not a copy of that one. Scope of this pack version: the CORE capability only -- Spark DSL extension (section/entity/schema), one transformer, one verifier, the generated Info module, and an Igniter installer that really patches the target module. Reactor-pipeline generation is included as an opt-in capability (workflow.reactor = true on the spec) using ash_r2rml's reactor_pipeline.ex/reactor/steps shape as the template, but is not required for every extension -- Ash's own guidance is that Reactor is for workflows needing real orchestration, not every extension. AshGraphql/AshJsonApi composition-fixture test generation follows ash_r2rml's test/ggen_api_bundle_test.exs pattern (live Code.compile_string + real Spark.Dsl.Extension Info-module introspection, ash_graphql/ash_json_api as :test-only deps -- never a runtime dependency, never a mock). Note: the per-target composition assertion currently only checks that the target library's own Info module exposes the expected function (function_exported?/3) -- it does not yet attach ash_graphql/ash_json_api to the generated fixture and introspect through them, so it confirms the library is present and shaped as expected, not that the generated extension actually composes with it. Tracked as a follow-up, not silently passed off as full composition coverage. Deferred to later pack versions (named here so they are visible next manufacturing edges, not silently dropped): ash-extension-composition-pack (dedicated multi-extension compatibility fixture matrix), ash-extension-starter-pack (composition/root pack selecting capabilities), ash_intelligence and ash_github (separate, larger packages -- out of scope for this pack). |
| [ash-extension-pack](../../packs/ash-extension-pack/) | projection | active | Canonical Ash-extension manufacturer for ggen-marketplace. This pack is the single reusable manufacturing surface for Ash/Spark extension semantics. It consolidates and supersedes ash-extension-core-pack and ash-extension-starter-pack. Those legacy generic manufacturers are retained only as lifecycle-marked superseded compatibility surfaces until consumer migration is evidenced; reusable Ash-extension discoveries extend this pack's capability families rather than creating sibling generic Ash packs. The governing search order is REUSE -> COMPOSE -> EXTEND -> INVENT. A new capability may be invented only when it is not in the closure of existing capability families, and the result is added here as a generalizable semantic capability rather than as another Ash-extension manufacturer. Spark is the semantic waist. Behaviorally meaningful extension semantics must be represented in Spark and consumed by the implementation: implementation_semantics - spark_semantics = empty spark_semantics - consumed_semantics = empty Explicitly admitted implementation mechanics may remain outside Spark only when they carry no independent domain/configuration semantics. The canonical pack also absorbs the late core-pack codegen callback, support-subdirectory, section metadata, entity description, and fixture-isolation semantics so consolidation is not lossy. It manufactures and qualifies composable capability families including Spark DSL sections/entities/schema, transformers, verifiers, Info/introspection, structured errors, Igniter installation, Reactor realization, context propagation, lifecycle/activation, durability/replay, observation/evidence, and knowledge/documentation projections. Frameworks such as Reactor, AshOban, AshStateMachine, Splode, and Igniter are qualified realizations of those capabilities, not private semantic authorities. Domain-specific packs (for example GraphLaw or R2RML projections) may remain separate when they carry independent semantic authority. Their reusable Ash projection patterns belong here; their domain ontologies do not. Vision 2040 planning and the no-pack-proliferation rule are specified in planning/vision2040.hddl and VISION_2040.md. Qualification includes structural courts, Spark<->implementation parity, mutation/falsifier courts, regeneration, composition, Igniter idempotence, Reactor fidelity, and temporal burn-in. A surviving reusable gap is fed back into this canonical pack and the manufacture cycle is rerun. Changelog (pack-local note; this pack records changes here -- no separate CHANGELOG.md): 0.5.0 (2026-10-04) -- absorbed the real, shipped ash_a2a A2A-projection DSL surface as a worked aex:AshA2aSpec fixture, transcribed from lib/ash_a2a/dsl.ex and lib/ash_a2a/verifiers/verify_skills.ex (main@5a84d886e0696cd43115799bbdc4bc8ec481376c) with verbatim per-fact aex:dslCitation rows: the :a2a section (skill entity with the three v26.10 fields argument_mapping/get?/lease_required?, nested argument + hddl_operator entities, semantic_requests option), the :authority section (gate/lease_duration_ms), and the :hooks section (pre_dispatch/post_dispatch). New templates/a2a_skill.ex.tmpl demonstrates the current grammar; gates/ 140_a2a_skill_fields_contract.rq refuses the three-field surface going stale and gates/150_a2a_dead_surface.rq refuses decorative (unconsumed) ash_a2a surface facts; gate 120's allowlist refreshed for the new aex:dslCitation property. |

Adds two REAL, review-confirmed capabilities core-pack's fixed ash_r2rml-derived shape does not yet cover, rather than duplicating what core-pack already has (an earlier draft of this pack wrongly re-invented core-pack's existing aex:workflowReactor/aex:CompositionTarget as a parallel `aexs:` vocabulary -- deleted after checking core-pack/ontology.ttl directly): 1. **Dynamic Reactor step-graph generation** (`templates/reactor_pipeline_dynamic.ex.tmpl`) -- core-pack's own `reactor_pipeline.ex.tmpl` hardcodes ash_r2rml's specific five-step pipeline body (compile_resources -> verify_alignment/evaluate_differential -> attach_provenance -> apply_policy -> render_r2rml_turtle). This pack's `aex:ReactorStep` class (ontology.ttl) lets a spec declare an ARBITRARY step graph, so a different extension's own pipeline shape (not ash_r2rml's specific five steps) can be generated. 2. **Receipted-action generation** (`templates/receipted_action.ex.tmpl`) -- a review of `/Users/sac/xaas` (2026-09-09, finding #5) found its real `Xaas.Actuation.run/4` (lib/xaas/actuation.ex:427-531) is architecturally distinct from core-pack's `workflowReactor`: idempotency-key-gated admission, a sealed-receipt entity, transaction-wrapped DO, and a deterministic-replay path -- exactly the shape `ex4pm`'s real `Evidence.BRCE.execute/5` (admit -> pending-receipt -> run -> outcome-receipt) already implements, and exactly what the ash_ex4pm extension's planned `brce_gate` capability (/tmp/ash_ex4pm_prfaq.md, this session) needs. `aex:generatesReceiptedAction` lets a spec opt into this shape. Disclosed as a first cut, not a byte-for-byte Actuation.run/4 port: it does not yet wrap the target action call in an explicit outer transaction the way xaas's own module does (see the template's own header comment) -- named follow-up, not silently claimed equivalent. **Tool-boundary disclosure (xaas review finding #4, real and previously paid-for in this environment -- see xaas/docs/case-studies/next-read/RCA-ggen-tool-confusion.md):** This pack, like ash-extension-core-pack, is driven by the Rust `ggen` binary (`ggen.toml` + Tera `.tmpl` templates with `sparql:`/`for_each:` frontmatter). It is UNRELATED to the Elixir `ggen_igniter` hex package (`mix ggen_igniter.sync --ontology/--query/--template/--out`, EEx templates, no `ggen.toml`), despite the similar name. A consumer whose own repo ALSO uses `ggen_igniter` for other generation (e.g. xaas's real `lib/mix/tasks/xaas.library.manufacture.ex`, generated by `ggen_igniter.sync --pack-dir`) must not assume this pack's templates run through that same tool -- they are rendered via `ggen sync run` against a `ggen.toml` pointing at this pack's (or core-pack's) `templates/` directory. Named follow-ups from the two review passes, deferred in this version (see ontology.ttl's own follow-up comment block for the full list with file:line citations): Reactor middleware declaration, transformer after?/before? ordering, verifier delegate-and-join-refusals idiom, Info module getter/getter!/predicate? triple, arbitrary N-length third-party-extension composition (xaas resources routinely stack 3-4 extensions -- AshJsonApi + AshGraphql + AshAdmin + AshAi on one domain, lib/xaas/library.ex:8 -- not just the ash_graphql/ash_json_api pair aex:CompositionTarget covers today), and a multi-phase orchestrating installer (ordered target list + `--phase` selector, matching xaas's real generated `xaas.library.manufacture` task shape). Verification status: ontology.ttl and both new templates are hand-reviewed against their cited real sources (ash_r2rml's reactor_pipeline.ex, xaas's actuation.ex) but NOT yet run through a real `ggen sync run` against a live spec fixture -- that is the next real step before this pack can be called ALIVE rather than UNVERIFIED. |

Fix, as bounded work: (1) new bpm:ashTypeExpr on every bpm:FieldType individual (datetime -> ":utc_datetime_usec", the other seven exactly as the ladder had them), so the Ash type is an ontology fact like erlangTypeExpr/elixirTypeExpr/gleamTypeExpr/jsonSchemaType; (2) new igniter/queries/ash_fields.rq -- fields.rq plus an OPTIONAL JOIN to the FieldType vocabulary for ?ash_type_expr and ?sample_elixir -- consumed ONLY by the two Ash templates, so fields.rq's other consumers (per-type doc pages, the cross-engine manifest probe) keep running on the consumer graph alone; the join is OPTIONAL and both templates raise BY RECORD AND FIELD NAME on an unbound ?ash_type_expr, so an unadmitted type, a FieldType lacking the property, or a consumer-only graph is a named render refusal (measured: consumer-only run exits 1 with zero files written), never a silently dropped attribute and never the old FunctionClauseError; (3) new gates/035_field_type_ash_expr.rq refuses a bpm:FieldType carrying anything but exactly one bpm:ashTypeExpr on the Rust `ggen sync run` leg too; (4) the test template's fixtures now come from the SAME bpm:sampleElixir the codec/roundtrip (GATE M5) templates render, and FieldType_datetime's codec/roundtrip sample* literals move to the six-microsecond-digit "2026-08-29T12:00:00.123456Z" (opaque binary()/String.t()/JSON string on those legs, so they round-trip unchanged); (5) the Ash identity relation for datetime is stated in the generated test and here as DateTime.compare(ash_read, DateTime.from_iso8601(wire)) == :eq over a normalized UTC %DateTime{} with microsecond {n, 6} -- explicitly NOT byte or struct identity (a no-fraction wire value parses {0, 0} but reads back {0, 6}; ".5Z" {500000, 1} vs {500000, 6}). Falsifier run: the regenerated ocel_event test against the pre-fix :utc_datetime resource fails with left: :lt; against the regenerated :utc_datetime_usec resource it passes. Note the engine contract this exposed: GgenIgniter.Query.Oxigraph returns PLAIN lexical values (Literal::value()), so the templates' historical raw-N-Triples quote-stripping norm/1 must not be applied to a sample literal that legitimately begins with a quote character -- the two new columns are read verbatim. Ash is still not exercised by beam4pm's scripts/roundtrip_check.sh (the M5 wire proof stays Erlang<->Elixir); the Ash leg's identity is proven per resource by its generated ExUnit test against the shared fixture, not by the cross-language wire script. v0.1.14 (2026-09-05): the "Deterministic sample values" comment block in beam4pm_roundtrip.ex.tmpl, beam4pm_roundtrip.erl.tmpl and beam4pm_codec_tests.erl.tmpl still hardcoded the pre-0.1.13 no-fraction datetime literal in prose while the generated code below it now carries the six-microsecond-digit vocabulary fixture -- a stale statement in generated output, caught by grepping the regenerated tree for the old literal. Comment lines only; no generated code changes. v0.1.15 (2026-09-05): the Ash projection joins the GATE M5 wire proof (VISION-2030 section 23 Polyglot BEAM). Two new igniter/ EEx recipe templates, both single-output on records + ash_fields.rq over the merged consumer+pack graph: beam4pm_ash_roundtrip.ex.eex renders BeamPM.AshRoundtrip, which for every admitted record type x {full, minimal} takes the SAME wire fixture the Erlang and Elixir legs exchange (the consumer's scripts/roundtrip_check.sh writes <record>.<variant>.erl.json / .ex.json), decodes it through BeamPM.Codec (the cross-engine path), creates the generated Ash.Resource on the real Ash.DataLayer.Ets, reads it back BY PRIMARY KEY (both variants of a record share one table per VM, so a read-all can never match one row) and compares field by field against BeamPM.Roundtrip.sample/2 -- the independent construction the other two legs compare against. The relation is stated precisely because BeamPM.Codec.to_map/1 does not apply to an Ash struct (to_known_map stringifies atoms; Ash reads atoms back): attributes whose bpm:ashTypeExpr is in the :utc_datetime family use DateTime.compare(ash_read, DateTime.from_iso8601(wire)) == :eq with nil == nil for an optional datetime absent from the minimal wire (DateTime.from_iso8601(nil) raises), every other attribute uses == against BOTH the sample and the codec-decoded struct, and the synthetic uuid_primary_key :id is disclosed as the only Ash-only public attribute and asserted so per record (a second Ash-only attribute is a named failure). Which attributes are datetime is an ontology fact rendered from ash_fields.rq (unbound ?ash_type_expr refused by record and field name, as in the two sibling Ash templates), and beam4pm_ash_roundtrip_test.exs.eex pins that fact against Ash.Resource.Info.attribute types at test time. That test template is the same-language ("ex") exercise: a full 578-fixture sweep, the :id-only disclosure over every resource, and two falsifiers run rather than reasoned -- a fixture with one datetime rewritten to the no-fraction form and one with a string mutated must each be refused naming record, variant and field (the tampered wire is self-consistent through Ash, so only comparison against the independent sample catches it). The test cleans its own ETS rows up (Ash.DataLayer.Ets.stop/1 per resource, waiting until :ets.whereis/1 reports the table gone) because the per-resource suite reads back with a one-row read-all. Scope disclosure, not a claim: Ash :string defaults (trim?: true, allow_empty?: false) mean whitespace-padded or empty strings would not round-trip identically on the Ash leg -- no fixture on any leg exercises that class, so the gate proves identity for the fixture class only, the same scope the Erlang/Elixir legs have always had. v0.1.16 (2026-09-05): observed vs inferred edges over tracing spans (VISION-2030 section 24 falsifier "telemetry adjacency cannot be distinguished from causality well enough for trustworthy process inference"; section 7 "observed" and "inferred" are distinct views of the twin). Measured before: every discovery projection (beam4pm_discovery.erl/ex/gleam.tmpl) derived directly-follows edges from TEMPORAL ADJACENCY only -- traces_from_events sorts by {event_time, event_id} and promotes every consecutive pair inside a case to a dfg_edge; no code path read a span parent/child link, and the consumer's admitted service_span carried no ordering field and no trace partition key, so the two evidence classes could not even be computed on the same input. The increment, all three sibling projections in lockstep (no Gleam divergence added): traces_from_spans/1 -- one log_trace per trace_id ordered by {start_time, span_id}, parent_span_id never read (the temporal-adjacency reading, deliberately the same dfg_from_traces code path event logs feed) -- and causal_dfg_from_spans/1, which returns {ok, %{observed, adjacent, inferred_only, observed_not_adjacent, orphans}}: observed = one edge per (parent service_name, child service_name) parent/child link with frequency = link count; adjacent = traces_from_spans -> dfg_from_traces re-tagged; inferred_only = adjacent pairs no link supports (what adjacency invented); observed_not_adjacent = linked pairs adjacency never produced (causality it cannot see) -- the two sets are NOT nested, so BOTH differences are returned; orphans = {span_id, parent_span_id} for every span whose parent is absent from the input, never an invented edge, never dropped, and still placed in the adjacency arm so missing evidence is distinguishable from invention. Typed refusals: {error, {duplicate_span_id, Id}} (an index would last-write-win) and {error, {parent_in_other_trace, ChildId}} (links never cross traces). The edges are a NEW admitted record shape the consumer declares, span_edge (source_service, target_service, frequency, evidence in {parent_child_link, temporal_adjacency} as a bpm:fieldType atom), deliberately not dfg_edge: an OpenTelemetry parent -> child link is invocation/containment causality (the child ran INSIDE the parent's interval), not directly-follows, and the evidence class must survive a caller merging the lists -- so it lives ON the record. Terminology pinned in every generated doc: parent/child links, never the distinct OpenTelemetry `links` field. Consumer-side manufacturing inputs this version expects: service_span gains trace_id (string, required) and start_time (datetime, required), span_edge is admitted; qualification/consumer.ttl carries both so the qualification render has the same accessor arities as the reference consumer. The discovery templates' schema-driven accessor list adds "service_span" and "span_edge" (erl) / the VALUES clause (ex, ex test); beam4pm_discovery.gleam.tmpl and beam4pm_gleam_test.tmpl now render the admitted record count from the records query instead of a stale hard-coded 35. This closes part of Ontology expressiveness/Target-API fidelity's L3 'error cases' gap that Round 3 explicitly left open, but stops short of L3 in full: no per-command error-path (which variant a given command actually raises) or exit-code facts are modeled -- only the shared enum-level contract, uniform across all rows. Round 5 (2026-07-21, L5 wave 5) closed the handler-gap dimension named in .specify/maturity.ttl's cg_010 mat:d2 ('L1 -- nothing callable, catalog only, no cargo-cicd invocation'): first checked directly (per the task's own instruction) whether this pack's existing generated proof (tests/cargo_cicd_catalog_proof.rs, the 15/15-passing artifact mat:d5 cites) hand-transcribes expected values the way praxis-core-pack/star-toml-pack's ORIGINAL proofs did -- it does not; both its `rows`/`error_variants` sparql: queries are byte-identical to the ones cargo_cicd_catalog.rs.tmpl already uses, rendered via a from-scratch Tera for-loop, so the cap05 gap this wave's instructions target does not apply here and no second proof template was added. Instead, following the fallback instruction, added a real subprocess dispatch shim mirroring mcpp-pack's src/mcpp_dispatch.rs.tmpl structure (read in full as the reference): cargo_cicd_dispatch.rs.tmpl generates src/cargo_cicd_dispatch.rs, one real std::process::Command-backed wrapper fn per live command (51 of 52 catalog rows -- the deprecated cc:doctor-bare row, cnv:verb "", is deliberately excluded via a second, independent `FILTER(?verb != "")` sparql: query, since `cargo-cicd doctor ""` is not a real invocation), invoking the real `cargo-cicd` binary directly (confirmed at ~/cargo-cicd/Cargo.toml's [[bin]] name = "cargo-cicd"; its own main.rs strip_cargo_subcommand_token only removes a leading "cicd" token when cargo itself injected one, so a direct `cargo-cicd <noun> <verb>` invocation reaches the identical clap parse `cargo cicd <noun> <verb>` would). cargo_cicd_dispatch_proof.rs.tmpl adds 9 real-behavior tests (Command::get_program/get_args introspection without spawning, plus two real ErrorKind::NotFound spawn-error tests guarded against a machine that happens to have cargo-cicd installed) -- mirroring mcpp_dispatch_proof.rs.tmpl's structure, with the per-wrapper existence/shape check driven by the same sparql: rows query as the dispatch shim itself (51 rows, not a hand-picked sample) so a dropped/renamed generated function fails to COMPILE, not merely fails an assertion. cargo_cicd_mod_wiring.rs.tmpl gained `pub mod cargo_cicd_dispatch;`. Live-verified end-to-end in a new committed consumer, examples/cargo-cicd-verify (real `ggen sync run` + `cargo test`, mirroring examples/praxis-core-verify's structure): 24/24 passing (15 catalog + 9 dispatch), a second sync byte-identical (idempotent), and drift-sensitivity proven via a real reversible ontology edit (renaming cc:git-status's cnv:verb from "status" to "statusdrift" and back) -- confirmed the generated wrapper fn renamed from git_status to git_statusdrift and back, AND surfaced a real, useful finding along the way: this pack's freeze_policy:checksum artifacts (all five: catalog, proof, reference doc, and now dispatch, dispatch-proof) do not silently auto-regenerate on ontology drift when the file is otherwise untouched -- ggen-engine's write.rs decision order means an unedited-but-now-stale file hits [FM-WRITE-005] 'exists with differing content; refusing silent clobber' rather than being rewritten, so picking up a real ontology change requires deleting the target file(s) (or a future `force: true` companion) before the next sync, not just running `ggen sync run` again; this is a fail-closed property already latent in every pre-Round-5 freeze_policy:checksum artifact this pack ships, not something Round 5 introduced. Still short of L3's 'common behaviors generated' bar: this is a *generic* dispatcher (shells out to the real binary) rather than a reimplementation of any command's actual behavior, so cargo-cicd's own logic still lives entirely in its own binary, not in ontology-specified logic -- matching mcpp-pack's own identically-scoped, already-disclosed limitation. (2) ~/cargo-cicd/src/nouns/ now contains 22 noun files, not 21: a new lsp.rs (added via commits 'feat(lsp): manufacture cargo-cicd-lsp workspace...' through 'fix(lsp): intercept lsp explain <CODE>...') defines a real #[verb("check")] command (`lsp check`) that postdates this pack's Round 5 (2026-07-21) audit and is not represented in ontology.ttl's 21-noun/52-row catalog (51 live + 1 deprecated cc:doctor-bare). This pack's "52 commands across 21 nouns" / "51 live rows" coverage claims are therefore no longer complete against the current target repo; the lsp noun is a known, disclosed gap not yet audited into the ontology. |

| [dogfood-lifecycle-pack](../../packs/dogfood-lifecycle-pack/) | projection | active | v26.7.13 Operation Dogfood session-lifecycle schema: the RDF vocabulary, SHACL shape, and sample fixtures for capturing a Claude Code session's tool events (Bash / Edit / Write / Read / Task / ...) as PROV-O provenance so that ggen can validate a session log. A PostToolUse hook appends one Turtle node per tool event and a session-end recipe runs `ggen graph validate --files <session.ttl> --shapes <shapes.ttl>`; this pack authors the vocabulary + shape + fixtures that loop targets (the hook and recipe themselves are wired by the parent session, not here). PUBLIC-ONTOLOGY-FIRST (mirrors packs/soc2-audit-pack and packs/dry-run-publish-pack): every relationship reuses a public vocabulary where one fits — prov: (Activity for the session and each tool event, Agent for the operator and subagents, used/generated/wasAssociatedWith/actedOnBehalfOf), dcterms: (identifier for the session id, isPartOf for the tool-event -> session ref, description), skos: (ConceptScheme + notation for the closed tool-name and outcome vocabularies), time: (inXSDDateTimeStamp for the wall-independent event timestamp). Content-addressed tool inputs/outputs use the repo's existing urn:blake3:<hex> scheme (crates/chatman-common provenance::content_address, crates/cng pipeline.rs ImportedArtifact). DISCLOSED MINTED TERMS (capability-justified, no public equivalent — each carries an rdfs:comment in ontology.ttl naming the checked public ontologies and why they do not fit): dfl:Session and dfl:ToolEvent (rdfs:subClassOf prov:Activity — PROV has no subtype distinguishing a session-scoped activity from a single tool invocation, and SHACL needs a precise sh:targetClass to require tool-event properties without imposing them on the session node); dfl:sequenceIndex (monotonic per-session ordinal — PROV has no event ordinal, OLO's olo:index requires full ordered-list slot membership); dfl:outcome + dfl:Outcome (a tool event's terminal status drawn from a CLOSED 3-value vocab ok/error/blocked — mirrors packs/jira-tracking-pack's closed jira:Status scheme; no public ontology enumerates tool-invocation outcomes). OBSERVATION-ONLY FENCE (structural, not merely stated): this pack MODELS the session lifecycle as observation/provenance; it never asserts authority, permission, or actuation — those are separate governed surfaces (admission, hooks, receipts in crates/praxis-graphlaw/src/chatman). No class, predicate, or individual here is named 'authorize', 'permit', 'grant', 'actuate', or 'execute'; the outcome vocabulary records what a tool event OBSERVABLY did (ok/error/blocked), never that it was permitted to. No external ontology is unioned — this pack's vocabulary is self-contained PROV/DCMI/SKOS/OWL-Time, so no ggen.toml extra_ontologies entry is required. No private namespace is minted beyond the disclosed capability-justified terms above. |
| [domain-capability-pack](../../packs/domain-capability-pack/) | projection | active | 80/20 ERRC answer to a real, found gap: a domain's capability/authority list (what an executable world exposes, and what a consuming pipeline is allowed to call) currently exists in multiple hand-authored, independently-drifting places with no shared vocabulary and no drift guard between them. Concrete instance proven this pack version (2026-08-11): SREGym's real capability surface. ~/gymact/src/gymact/gyms/sregym.py::SREGYM_CAPABILITIES declares 14 real capabilities (all Consequence.DO -- observe_cluster_state, run_kubectl, submit_diagnosis, submit_mitigation, get_benchmark_status, jaeger_get_services/get_operations/get_traces/get_dependency_graph, loki_get_logs/get_labels/get_label_values, prometheus_get_metrics/get_alerts). ~/autofde-lab/src/autofde_lab/fabric/gymact_capabilities.toml hand-maintains a 5-entry allowlist subset of that same set for autofde-lab's own diagnosing pipeline -- and its own in-file comment currently asserts "5 entries; there is no jaeger/loki/prometheus capability in the real gymact source -- only these 5 exist", which is now FALSE against the real, currently-installed gymact source (confirmed directly, 2026-08-11): the real source has grown to 14. This is not a hypothetical failure mode this pack guards against -- it is a real, already-happened instance of exactly the drift this pack's gates exist to catch, found while authoring this pack, not invented as a motivating example. This pack does not fix that drift (fixing gymact_capabilities.toml to be GENERATED from this pack's admitted facts is out of scope for this version -- named follow-up, lives in a different repo). It provides the shared vocabulary (dcp:Capability / dcp:LabAllowlist / dcp:CapabilitySourceManifest) and the two gates (exact-count-per-source, allowlist-subset-of-domain) that would have caught the drift above mechanically, the moment gymact's real capability count diverged from the allowlist's assumption -- and it admits the real, current 14-capability / 5-entry-allowlist facts as a worked instance, not an empty template. ERRC vocabulary (errc:Finding) reused verbatim from packs/gh-actions-errc-pack -- deliberately NOT reinvented a third time (packs/pack-authoring-pack's errc-testing-pattern.md already uses a different, markdown-blob shape; this pack picks the richer, SPARQL-queryable gh-actions-errc-pack shape instead of adding a fourth). aa:Capability's proof-surface discipline (positive execution / negative refusal / receipt-replay, packs/automatic-autonomic-operations-pack) is the acknowledged precedent for this pack's count/uniqueness gate pattern, generalized here past ggen's own kernel to an arbitrary external domain's capability list, keyed by (sourceRepo, sourceFile) rather than one hardcoded global magic number -- so a second domain instance (a different gym, a different lab pipeline) is an additive fact set, not a rewrite of this pack's gates. v0.2.0 (2026-09-30, capability-ecology wave lane 1): the DOMAIN-family contract layer. The namespace moved verbatim to the pinned https://ggen.dev/ontology/domain-capability# (per-term dcterms:isReplacedBy records in ontology.ttl; nothing deleted or renamed silently). New: dcp:DomainCapability (stable semantic identity carrying the pinned dotted IDs Domain.Action.Invoke / Domain.Query.Read / Domain.Change.Apply via rdfs:label + dcterms:identifier) and dcp:Realization (a qualified capability version, composed with packs/qualified-capability-ecology-pack's qce:QualifiedCapability lifecycle, bound to its identity through the one missing qce: edge, dcp:realizes). Capabilities express inputs, outputs, preconditions, postconditions, outcome sets (success + typed failures + nondeterministic), evidence kinds, authority requirements (closed none/observe/construct, never do), and execution properties. Realizations name only modules actually read this session (Ash.Reactor.{Read,ReadOne,Create,Update,Destroy,BulkCreate,BulkUpdate,BulkDestroy, Action}Step, AshPPlan.Providers.Steps.DomainAction, Ash.CodeInterface, Ash.bulk_*/4) with real sha256 artifact digests and provider/version-pin metadata. Six new refusal gates encode the invariants: capability-without-realization, realization-without-qualification-conditions, ProviderAvailable != Authorized, Policy != Authority (no DO authority), Plan != Execution (runtime episodes execute only frozen realizations), and contract required-fields. Every new gate has a positive-clean and a witnessed-firing negative fixture (qualification/fixtures/, run by qualification/verify.py; pinned by tests/test_domain_capability_pack.py). |

| [dspy-pack](../../packs/dspy-pack/) | projection | active | Universal DSPy generation vocabulary, verified against the real installed dspy 3.1.3 source tree (not docs prose) via inspect.signature() on every admitted constructor and compile() method, and real object construction/execution against actual dspy classes. Pure law -- ontology.ttl ships zero individuals, so composing this pack cannot inject any signature, module, or optimizer into a consumer's generated src/dspy_program.py / src/dspy_optimize.py. A consumer project supplies its own individuals against this vocabulary in its own .ttl. dspy:Signature/InputField/OutputField -- typed fields admit a primitive dspy:pythonType (str/int/float/bool), a Literal[...]/List[Literal[...]] enum (dspy:hasLiteralOption), int ge/le bounds (dspy:geInt/leInt), or a generated pydantic.BaseModel type (dspy:hasPydanticModelType) -- exactly one of the three per field. dspy:Module -- 13 of dspy 3.1.3's real Module classes: Predict, ChainOfThought, ReAct (with dspy:usesMCPServer -> dspy:MCPServerConnection for MCP tool discovery, per dspy.ai's "DSPy + MCP" tutorial), ProgramOfThought, MultiChainComparison, RLM, CodeAct (with dspy:hasLocalTool scaffolded stubs), BestOfN/Refine (which wrap another Module via dspy:wrapsModule instead of a Signature), Pipeline (an ordered linear composition of steps with real data-flow ArgBindings -- the verified retrieve-then-reason/RAG pattern), MultiHop (a fixed, parameterized query-gen/retrieve/accumulate-context/answer-gen recipe, also verified by real execution), and KNN/Parallel (previously excluded -- see below). dspy:Optimizer -- 16 of dspy 3.1.3's real Teleprompter subclasses: GEPA, GRPO, BootstrapFewShot, BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch, BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna, BootstrapFinetune, COPRO, SignatureOptimizer, MIPROv2, AvatarOptimizer, BetterTogether (wraps another Optimizer via dspy:wrapsPromptOptimizer/wrapsWeightOptimizer), InferRules, SIMBA, LabeledFewShot, Ensemble (previously excluded -- see below), KNNFewShot (previously excluded -- see below). Each optimizer's real, per-kind constructor AND compile() parameter names are followed exactly -- these vary meaningfully (SignatureOptimizer's compile() takes devset= not trainset=; COPRO/ SignatureOptimizer require an eval_kwargs dict; BootstrapFewShotWithOptuna's compile() requires max_demos). Three real UPSTREAM dspy 3.1.3 defects are documented as caveats directly on the relevant ontology properties (not hidden): SignatureOptimizer is unexported and its deprecated shim is broken; AvatarOptimizer calls a removed dspy.TypedPredictor; BetterTogether has a narrower runtime optimizer whitelist than its type signature suggests. 2026-08-10: composition/retrieval/KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot support added, closing every gap the pack previously excluded. dspy.Retrieve, the retrieve-then-reason (RAG) pattern, the 2-hop query-gen/retrieve/accumulate/answer-gen loop, and dspy.KNN/dspy.Parallel/dspy.Ensemble/ dspy.KNNFewShot construction+execution were each actually built and run against the real installed dspy 3.1.3 (not assumed from docs) -- see dspy:PipelineStep/dspy:ArgBinding, dspy:EmbedderConfig, and the "MultiHop"/"Pipeline"/"KNN"/"Parallel"/"Ensemble"/"KNNFewShot" dspy:kind values. dspy.Assert/dspy.Suggest were investigated and found fully removed from dspy 3.x -- dspy:Refine/dspy:BestOfN, already modeled, are confirmed dspy's complete modern replacement; no new construct was needed for that axis. Metric/reward/reduce function BODIES, tool bodies, and trainset/valset/devset/eval_kwargs contents are deliberately out of ontology scope (arbitrary, consumer-owned inputs) -- ggen scaffolds NotImplementedError stubs and named placeholders in src/dspy_program.py / src/dspy_optimize.py. Covers dspy.ai's own tutorials verbatim (fetched/verified 2026-08-10): general Predict/ ChainOfThought modeling, MCP tool use (https://dspy.ai/tutorials/mcp/), GEPA optimization (https://dspy.ai/tutorials/gepa_ai_program/), RL/GRPO optimization (https://dspy.ai/tutorials/rl_ai_program/), two GEPA worked examples -- gepa_facilitysupportanalyzer (Literal/List[Literal] enum fields) and gepa_trusted_monitor (int ge/le bounds) -- plus the retrieve-then-reason RAG pattern and 2-hop multi-hop pattern (both directly executed against dspy.utils.dummies.DummyLM/dummy_rm this session). Fourteen real, generated-and-tested example fixtures (ontology.ttl + ggen.toml, one per fixture family: MCP/ReAct, GEPA Literal fields, all 9 original Module kinds, three optimizer families, Pydantic model fields, Pipeline/RAG, MultiHop, KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot, plus a 4-fixture "playground" set of dspy's most common tutorial-first patterns -- bare-Predict QA, ChainOfThought math reasoning with a typed float output, Literal-constrained classification, ChainOfThought summarization) live in the ggen monorepo's own examples/<name>/ directories and are wired into that repo's `cargo test` suite (crates/ggen-engine/tests/dspy_pack_e2e.rs) -- each verified this pack version by running the real `ggen sync` pipeline and constructing/executing the real generated dspy objects with zero exceptions (Pipeline/MultiHop/KNN/Parallel/Ensemble/KNNFewShot and all four playground fixtures additionally verified by real Python execution against dspy 3.1.3, not just by inspecting the rendered source text). |
| [dsrust-pack](../../packs/dsrust-pack/) | projection | active | Universal DsRust generation vocabulary grounded in seanchatmangpt/dsrust at exact source commit f24adde08c1d8850e4d7079d019643bb40f905cb (crate 0.1.0-alpha.2). This is the Rust-native counterpart to dspy-pack: consumers declare signatures, modules, agent tools, execution policies, and optimizers as RDF; ggen projects them into Rust construction code without granting generated code ambient execution authority. Admitted Module implementors at that commit are Predict, ChainOfThought, ReAct, ReActV2, MultiChainComparison, BestOfN, and Refine. Parallel is also fully supported, but source-grounded as an ExecutionPolicy because dsrust::Parallel does not implement dsrust::Module; it constructs a bounded helper whose run() consumes consumer-supplied (&dyn Module, Example) work. Admitted optimizer kinds are exactly LabeledFewShot, BootstrapFewShot, COPRO, MIPROv2, and GEPA. The gates fail closed for DSPy constructs not exported by DsRust at the admitted source identity (including ProgramOfThought, CodeAct, RLM, retrieval/KNN, Ensemble, and KNNFewShot) rather than manufacturing fictional Rust APIs. Arbitrary tool bodies, reward bodies, metric bodies, trainset contents, Parallel work items, and provider credentials are consumer-owned authority. ggen therefore emits explicit panic/error seams for executable consumer bodies and construction-only helpers for execution policies. Generated construction can be compiled by a consumer, but marketplace qualification does not actuate a model, tool, optimizer, or Parallel workload. Version 0.2 adds an optional Fortune-5 enterprise binding plane. It reuses the marketplace's existing fortune5-architecture vocabulary by reference, keeps enterprise governance separate from portable DSPy semantics, validates source/authority/promotion/rollback/receipt boundaries when a binding is declared, and generates an architecture control matrix for review boards and production onboarding. Runtime identity, secrets, network, observability, SLO/DR, model data residency, and deployment controls remain owned by the consuming application and its enterprise architecture program. |

| [elixir-mcp-a2a-pack](../../packs/elixir-mcp-a2a-pack/) | projection | active | Generates a real Elixir MCP router scope + A2A agent module + capability descriptor from one admitted ema:CapabilitySurface, so xaas/ex4pm/beam4pm (or any future Ash app) can each stand up their own MCP/A2A surface from their own capability list instead of hand-writing router/agent boilerplate per repo -- built in direct response to the user's request (2026-09-09): "get the mcp/a2a side here ready ... elixir mcp/a2a in the packs so each system can spin the capabilities up instantly." Checked first for an existing pack covering this (Research Sources doctrine -- search manufacturing capital before writing consumer-local code): the marketplace already has rmcp-pack/mcpp-pack/fastmcp-pack/gym-mcp-surface-pack (all Rust or Python-targeted) and beam4pm-contracts-pack (mcp family) (Erlang codec contracts, not a live Elixir MCP server) and certification-assist-pack's protocol/*.json.tmpl (static JSON contract shape, no generated code). None generate a real, running Elixir `AshAi.Mcp.Router` forward or A2A agent module. This pack fills exactly that gap. No external ontology file is unioned via ggen.toml extra_ontologies; every FIBO/Commons/ODRL/PROV/DCMI term is reused directly by IRI, never re-vendored or re-serialized into this pack. This pack carries the CONTRACT half of the ALOOP-ZCODE-DOGFOOD-001 provider-neutrality law: WorkOrder identity, authority, planner, acceptance, receipt-schema and replay carry NO provider identity -- provider appears only as the left segment of a capabilityId ("provider:id") and in the provider's own runtime descriptor (capabilities, transport, availability, cost, concurrency, authority ceiling, receipt protocol). PUBLIC vocabulary first: ExecutionProvider is a prov:SoftwareAgent subclass, the request/receipt/capability spine is prov:Entity/Activity, metadata via dcterms, and the receipt field names are the ALOOP ExecutionReceipt contract verbatim (workOrderId, originAuthority, provider, providerExecutionId, subjectBefore, subjectAfter, commands, consequences, evidence, exitStatus, timestamps, replayBinding). COMPOSITION: with packs/aloop-episode-ontology-pack wired, a consumer dual-types its work orders (pec:WorkOrder alongside aloop:WorkOrder) and the two gate sets compose over one graph; this pack stands alone without it (zero cross-pack IRIs in gates/ or ontology.ttl). Anti-vacuity fixtures ship under qualification/fixtures/ (neg-* must fire, pos-* must be clean). Authority boundary: contract description and admission gates ONLY. NOT claimed: any actuation authority (describing an ExecutionProvider does not authorize one), provider selection POLICY (the gates enforce totality of routing, never which provider wins), cancellation authority (pec:Cancellation DESCRIBES an extinction event; executing one is outside this pack), or receipt validation of provider-specific payloads (gate 030 checks the 12 contract fields, nothing deeper). Consumers mint their own request/provider/receipt individuals; this pack ships zero consumer individuals except the dogfood provider/request/receipt triple named in ontology.ttl that witnesses the gates clean. |

The opt-in `--require-durable [--repo-map owner/repo=path ...]` profile closes the dead identity check (validate_receipt.py:20-25 probes subject_sha only when identity.repo is a local directory, and since V23-S it is the GitHub slug): identity.repo must be a mapped owner/repo slug whose repository holds identity.subject_sha (R_missing_identity), and replay.durable_location must be git-notes:refs/notes/<ref>@<sha>, git:<owner/repo>@<sha>:<path> (blob present, subject_sha equal to <sha> or its ancestor) or an https URL (form only), never an absolute local path (R_missing_replay). Generator vocabulary added: array forms (rp:minItems, rp:itemJsonType, rp:itemPattern), rp:minLength, rp:admitsIntegralFloat, rp:nullable, conditional requirement (rp:requiredWhenPath/Pattern), rp:ImplicationRule, per-binding rp:brokenTerm, rp:Profile, and rp:ResolutionKind read-only git probes (subject_commit, notes_object, blob_at_commit, ancestor_of). With no flag every verdict of the five earlier contracts is unchanged. No chatman_root_v1 contract: chatman crates/ecosystem-core Receipt::verify owns that one. Historical (2026-09-06, ggen 26.8.28, before dfcm_fleet_v1): `ggen sync run` writes both files (graph_hash 8737195c..., closure recorded); second run reports `skipped: unchanged: content identical` for the matrix. The generated validator reaches 4/4 exit-code parity with the REAL hand-written scripts/verify-receipt.sh across valid / bad-sha1 / missing-mandatory-field / sentinel-value-under-ALIVE fixtures, and returns VALID on the two real receipts on disk (artifacts/autonomic-crown.json, 13 submodule elements checked per-element; receipts/bootstrap-ggen-ecosystem-sync.json) -- neither of which has any validator today. Falsified, not just asserted: mutating one submodule SHA to 'NOTASHA' and one default_ref from refs/heads/main to 'main' both produce exit 1 with the exact failing value-form and its source file. Measured divergence recorded as a dqv:Consistency annotation, not an opinion: the SAME standing token is mutually invalid across the two repos. `REFUSED[MARKETPLACE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH]` passes verify-receipt.sh (exit 0) and fails clean_session (exit 1); `REFUSED:MARKETPLACE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` fails verify-receipt.sh (exit 1) and passes clean_session (exit 0) -- a perfect XOR, so no receipt can express a typed refusal that both repos accept. Authority boundary (see PROVENANCE.md, gates/01_no_actuation.rq, gates/05_probes_read_only.rq): read-only predicate + read-only git probes (git cat-file -e, git merge-base --is-ancestor, git notes --ref=R list) + data census. Writes nothing, admits nothing; consequential DO stays behind GymAct/BRCE. NOT claimed: subsumption of receipt_store.verify_chain's chain-link re-derivation (an algorithm over an ordered ledger, out of field-shape scope), verify-receipt.sh parity beyond the 4 exercised fixtures, validate_receipt.py parity beyond the receipts and fixtures exercised by the MP-RPV gate and generated/qualification_runner.py, any network probe of an https location, or any adoption -- this pack is purely additive and modifies no existing pack, script, schema, or receipt. |

only the pipe/@@ delimiter grammar is reused, not the column count, and this discrepancy is disclosed in ontology.ttl's own rmcp:macroFields comment rather than silently forced to 4 columns), rmcp:Transport (7 -- stdio, TokioChildProcess, StreamableHttpClientTransport [really a `pub type ... = WorkerTransport<StreamableHttpClientWorker<C>>` alias, not a struct -- disclosed], StreamableHttpService, WorkerTransport, AsyncRwTransport, SinkStreamTransport, each with its real feature gate read directly from src/transport.rs's own #[cfg(feature = ...)] attributes; SinkStreamTransport has none at all -- unconditionally compiled -- and its featureFlag value says so explicitly rather than being left empty or naming a fake feature), and rmcp:Feature (15 -- the 6+6+3 flags README.md's own three real markdown tables document; Cargo.toml itself defines 26 total, 11 more, undocumented in README and out of this pass's scope: __reqwest, local, auth-client-credentials-jwt, client-side-sse, server-side-http, tower, transport-worker, transport-streamable-http-server-session, transport-streamable-http-client-unix-socket, which-command, plus the implicit base64 optional-dependency feature -- the last one a real, disclosed fidelity gap: Cargo.toml's actual default array is ["base64", "macros", "server"], but README's own Feature Flags table has no base64 row and marks only server/macros as default, so rmcp:featureDefault reflects README's own (incomplete) default column, not the full Cargo.toml array). Two more templates were added during L5 pack-promotion capability closure (2026-07-21): tests/rmcp_handler_catalog_sparql_derived_proof.rs (cap05 -- "Generated verification": a SECOND, independent proof over rmcp:HandlerMethod, alongside the hand-transcribed one, carrying its own real sparql: frontmatter -- identical server_rows/client_rows queries to rmcp_handler_catalog.rs.tmpl -- with no freeze_policy of its own, re-baking LIVE_SERVER_ROWS/LIVE_CLIENT_ROWS fresh every sync and asserting them against src/rmcp_handler_catalog.rs's actual on-disk text via include_str!, reapplying star-toml-pack/praxis-core-pack's wave-2 reference pattern; drift-sensitivity verified live by temporarily editing rmcp:server-call-tool's rmcp:defaultBehavior and re-syncing -- the old hand-transcribed proof failed exactly as predicted while this one stayed green against the changed live value) and tests/rmcp_default_handler_proof.rs (cap06 -- "Generated negative witnesses": a real refusal-path/adversarial-input proof defining RmcpDefaultHandler with ZERO method overrides -- impl ServerHandler for RmcpDefaultHandler {} compiles because rmcp-2.2.0's own src/handler/server.rs:432-434 declares the entire trait body as one server_handler_methods!() macro invocation -- then calling its real, sync, zero-scaffolding get_tool() default body and asserting it genuinely returns None for an unregistered name, an empty name, and an adversarial path-traversal/injection-shaped name against the actual compiled rmcp crate, not a mock; a dropped get_tool individual would be a hard compile failure, covering the compile-fail sub-modality too). All 5 primary generated Rust/doc artifacts use freeze_policy: checksum (not force:true): a hand-edited output is refused with a named checksum-mismatch error on the next sync, not silently overwritten; the two new cap05/cap06 proof templates deliberately carry no freeze_policy (same reasoning as star-toml-pack's own cap05 template -- see its own docstring). gates/ (010_required.rq, 020_single_valued.rq, 030_value_constraints.rq) are SPARQL-translated-SHACL constraints, namespace-scoped to the rmcp# IRI space (same rationale as mcpp-pack's own gates: an unscoped gate would wrongly demand rmcp-only facts from other packs' individuals in a union graph), each carrying a `# MESSAGE:` comment naming the real constraint it translates. | [supabase-pack](../../packs/supabase-pack/) | projection | active | Projects the standard Supabase client/config wiring for any Node.js project (Next.js, Nuxt, Expo, plain Node backend) from admitted RDF facts about a Supabase project, its client runtimes, its tables, and its auth providers. Grounded in real usage patterns mined from ~14 real local projects on this machine using @supabase/supabase-js 2.38-2.108 (Next.js apps, Nuxt apps, Expo/React Native apps, and plain Node backends). Two findings from that mining shaped the pack's default: 1. The dominant real client pattern is a single-instance `createClient()` call in a small singleton module (`lib/supabase.ts` or a dedicated `packages/supabase` module), NOT the `@supabase/ssr` cookie-based dual client/server pattern -- `@supabase/ssr` showed up only as a transitive lockfile entry in a few projects, never as real imported source, and `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` had zero real usage anywhere scanned. This pack therefore defaults `sb:Client.package` to "@supabase/supabase-js" and generates a plain singleton client; `@supabase/ssr` dual client/server generation is available opt-in per `sb:Client` when `runtime` is set to "server" or "edge" alongside `package = "@supabase/ssr"`, for projects that do want Next.js App Router SSR auth. 2. Real environment variable names split by target: Node/backend projects overwhelmingly use bare `SUPABASE_URL` / `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` / `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`; Expo/React Native projects use the `EXPO_PUBLIC_` prefix required for Expo's public env var convention; a smaller minority of Next.js projects use `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. This pack projects the env var prefix from `sb:Client.runtime` and an explicit `sb:Project.envPrefix` fact rather than assuming one framework's convention project-wide. Every real migration file sampled enables RLS with `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and defines policies keyed on `auth.uid()` or `auth.role() = 'service_role'` -- this pack's gate `030_rls_requires_policy.rq` mirrors that discipline: any `sb:Table` with `hasRLS = true` and zero declared `sb:Policy` is refused. Verification practice: run `ggen sync run --dry-run` twice; the second run must report zero pending writes. |
